findings.title: Lack of Event Emission
findings.description: The Fusion Swap and Whitelist programs do not emit any events upon execution of their instructions. This omission significantly reduces the transparency and observability of on-chain state changes such as order creation, filling, or cancellation. The root cause is the deliberate design choice not to include event emissions in the code, likely to minimize compute unit (CU) usage. Without emitted events, external systems like indexers, dashboards, and integrator smart contracts must rely on complex and fragile transaction parsing logic to infer state changes, increasing development overhead and the risk of misinterpretation. The impact is a degraded developer and user experience, reduced protocol transparency, and increased difficulty in building reliable off-chain tooling, which may hinder ecosystem adoption and monitoring capabilities.

findings.title: Lack of External Documentation
findings.description: The solana-fusion-protocol repository lacks essential external documentation, including a README.md file, project description, setup instructions, and usage guides. This absence stems from the project maintainers not having prioritized documentation in the audited version. As a result, new contributors, auditors, and developers integrating with the protocol face significant barriers to understanding the system's architecture, dependencies, and operation. The lack of documentation reduces codebase accessibility, increases the risk of misuse, and undermines project credibility. While not a direct security vulnerability, it negatively impacts maintainability, auditability, and long-term sustainability, potentially leading to integration errors or misconfigurations by third parties.
